==English== {{wp}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/pɪt͡ʃ/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-pitch.ogg|a=US}} * {{audio|en|en-au-pitch.ogg|a=AU}} * {{rhymes|en|ɪtʃ|s=1}} ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*peyH-}} From {{inh|en|enm|picche}}, {{m|enm|piche}}, {{m|enm|pich}}, from {{inh|en|ang|piċ}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*pik}}, from {{der|en|la|pix}}. Cognate with {{cog|grc|πίσσα||pitch, tar}}, {{cog|la|pīnus||pine}}. More at {{m|en|pine}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|Pik|t=pitch, tar}}, {{cog|nl|pek|t=pitch, tar}}, {{cog|nds-de|Pick|t=pitch, tar}}, {{cog|de|Pech|t=pitch, tar}}, {{cog|ca|pega|t=pitch}}, {{cog|es|pegar||to stick, glue}}, {{cog|frp|pouatche||sap from a pine}} and {{cog|fr|poix||sap}}. The adjective is probably back-formed from {{m|en|pitch-black}}, reinterpreting "pitch" as meaning "intense(ly)". ====Noun==== {{en-noun|~}} # {{senseid|en|Q840692}} A [[sticky]], [[gummy]] substance secreted by trees; [[tree sap]]. #: {{ux|en|It is hard to get this '''pitch''' off my hand.}} ## Anything similar to or derived from tree sap: [[resin]]; [[rosin]]. # A [[dark]], extremely [[viscous]] material still remaining after [[distill]]ing [[crude oil]] or natural [[tar]]. #: {{nearsyn|en|tar|coal tar|asphalt|bitumen}} #: {{ux|en|They put '''pitch''' on the mast to protect it.}} #: {{ux|en|The barrel was sealed with '''pitch'''.}} #: {{ux|en|It was '''pitch''' black because there was no moon.}} # {{lb|en|geology}} [[pitchstone|Pitchstone]]. =====Derived terms===== {{col5|en |Burgundy pitch|pitchcapping|pitchless|pitchlike |Canada pitch |dark as pitch |Greek pitch |pitch mining |pitch moth |earth pitch |Jews' pitch |pitch apple |pitch-black |pitch black |pitchblende |pitch coal |pitch-dark |pitch dark |pitch darkness |pitch peat |pitch pine |the devil to pay and no pitch hot or ready |pitch-tar }} =====Descendants===== * {{desc|gl|piche|bor=1}} * {{desc|pt|piche|bor=1}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|sticky, gummy substance secreted by trees}} * Albanian: * Armenian: * Bashkir: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Chinook Jargon: * Czech: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * Georgian: * German: * Greek: * Hungarian: * Ingrian: * Italian: * Ladin: * Miwok: * Nanai: * Navajo: * Norwegian: * Occitan: * Persian: * Picard: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|смола́}} * Slovak: * Southern Altai: * Spanish: * Tagalog: * Turkish: * Venetan: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|dark, extremely viscous material made by distilling tar}} * Afrikaans: * Albanian: * Arabic: * Armenian: * Bashkir: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Czech: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * Georgian: * German: * Greek: * Hebrew: * Hungarian: * Ingrian: * Irish: * Italian: * Kurdish: * Latin: * Latvian: * Māori: * Norwegian: * Occitan: * Ojibwe: * Picard: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|дёготь|m}}, {{t+|ru|пек|m}} * Scottish Gaelic: * Serbo-Croatian: * Slovak: * Southern Altai: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Turkish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-see|pitchstone}} =====See also===== * {{l|en|piceous}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # To cover or smear with pitch. #* {{RQ:KJV|Genesis|6|14|passage=“Make thee an ark of gopher wood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt '''pitch''' it within and without with pitch.”}} # To [[darken]]; to [[blacken]]; to [[obscure]]. #* '''1704''' (published), year written unknown, {{w|John Dryden}}, ''On the Death of Amyntas'' ====Adjective==== {{en-adj|er}} # Very dark [[black]]; [[pitch-black]]. #* {{see citations|en}} # {{lb|en|of a|black color}} Intense, deep, dark. #* {{quote-book|en|date=2008-07-15|author=Edward Morgan Forster|author2=Christopher Isherwood|title=Letters Between Forster and Isherwood on Homosexuality and Literature|publisher=Palgrave MacMillan |text=Then I got back here - difficulty again: no trolly-bus, and black '''pitcher''' than black - and have since been conning the Beveridge Report.}} #* {{quote-book|en|date=2013-02-26|author=Dale E. Basye|title=Snivel: The Fifth Circle of Heck|publisher=Yearling|isbn=9780375868061|page=162 |text=If you lose even once, that's it: The screen goes, like, the '''pitchest''' black ever, and you're [out].}} #* {{quote-book|en|date=2016-08-30|author=Mandy Arioto|title=Starry-Eyed: Seeing Grace in the Unfolding Constellation of Life and Motherhood|publisher=Zondervan|isbn=9780310340362|page=19 |text=For some of us postpartum depression is the '''pitchest''' black we have ever known. From the dark womb we welcome new life, and our own new life, a life we haven't known, unfolds{{nb...}}}} #* {{see more citations|en|pitchest-black}} ===Etymology 2=== From {{der|en|enm|picchen}}, {{m|enm|pycchen|t=to thrust in, fasten, settle}}, from {{inh|en|ang|*piċċan}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*pikkijan}}, a variant of {{cog|gmw-pro|*pikkōn|t=to pick, peck}}, whence {{cog|enm|pikken}}, {{m|enm|picken|t=to pick, pierce}}, modern {{cog|en|pick}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun|~}} # A [[throw]]; a [[toss]]; a [[cast]], as of something from the hand. #: {{ux|en|a good '''pitch''' in quoits}} # {{senseid|en|the act of pitching a baseball}}{{lb|en|baseball}} The act of pitching a baseball. #: {{ux|en|The '''pitch''' was low and inside.}} # {{senseid|en|Q2310214}} {{lb|en|sports|UK|Australia|NZ}} The field on which [[cricket]], [[soccer]], [[rugby]], [[gridiron]] or [[hockey|field hockey]] is played. {{q|In cricket, the pitch is in the centre of the field; see {{m|en|cricket pitch}}.}} {{q|Not often used in the US or Canada, where "[[field]]" is the preferred word.}} #: {{ux|en|The teams met on the '''pitch'''.}} # {{lb|en|golf}} A short, high, lofty shot that lands with backspin. # {{lb|en|rare}} The field of battle. #* {{quote-book|en |year=1845 |author=Owen Connellan |title=Annals of Ireland: Translated from the Original Irish of the Four Masters |url= https://www.google.co.uk/books/edition/The_annals_of_Ireland_tr_from_the_orig_I/ggAIAAAAQAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=“pitch+of+battle”&pg=PA179&printsec=frontcover |page=179 |passage=“The two men of Alltraighe maintain, Two chiefs of the plain of Kerry, A clan the most active in '''pitch''' of battle, Their chiefs are O’Neide and Clan Conary.”}} #* {{quote-book|en |year=2015 |author=SK Benton |title=Lives of Future-Past |url= https://www.google.co.uk/books/edition/Lives_of_Future_Past/iqw7BwAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=“on+the+battle+pitch”&pg=PT153&printsec=frontcover |page= |passage=Every other day they would spend half of the training hours on the battle '''pitch'''.}} #* {{quote-book|en |year=2018 |author=Christopher R. Lakey |title=Sculptural Seeing: Relief, Optics and the Rise of Perspectives in Medieval Italy |url= https://www.google.co.uk/books/edition/Sculptural_Seeing/ZnNsDwAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=“on+the+battle+pitch”&pg=PA84&printsec=frontcover |page=84 |passage=George’s cult was popular in the east because of his legendary feats on the battle '''pitch''' and because of the location of his tomb, which was a pilgrimage site.}} # An effort to [[sell]] or [[promote]] something. #: {{ux|en|He gave me a sales '''pitch'''.}} # {{senseid|en|distance}}The [[distance]] between evenly spaced objects, e.g. the [[teeth]] of a [[saw]] or gear, the turns of a screw thread, the centres of holes, or [[letters]] in a [[monospace]] [[font]]. #: {{ux|en|The '''pitch''' of pixels on the point scale is 72 pixels per inch.}} #: {{ux|en|The '''pitch''' of this saw is perfect for that type of wood.}} #: {{ux|en|A helical scan with a '''pitch''' of zero is equivalent to constant z-axis scanning.}} # The [[angle]] at which an object sits. #: {{ux|en|the '''pitch''' of the roof or haystack}} # {{senseid|en|rot-angle}} The [[rotation]] angle about the [[transverse]] axis. ## {{lb|en|nautical|aviation}} The degree to which a vehicle, especially a ship or aircraft, rotates on such an axis, tilting its bow or nose up or down. ##: {{cot|en|roll#English:_rot-angle|yaw#English:_rot-angle|;|heave#Noun}} ##: {{ux|en|the '''pitch''' of an aircraft}} ## {{lb|en|aviation}} A measure of the [[angle of attack]] of a [[propeller]]. ##: {{ux|en|The propeller blades' '''pitch''' went to 90° as the engine was feathered.}} # An area in a market (or similar) allocated to a particular trader. # {{lb|en|by extension}} The place where a [[busker]] performs, a [[prostitute]] solicits clients, or an illegal gambling game etc. is set up before the public. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1975|author=Tom A. Cullen|title=The Prostitutes' Padre|page=94 |passage=Another reason is that the prostitute who makes her '''pitch''' at Marble Arch stands a chance of being picked up by an out-of-town business man stopping at one of the hotels in the vicinity, and of being treated to a steak dinner {{...}}}} # An area on a [[campsite]] intended for occupation by a single [[tent]], [[caravan]] or similar. # A [[level]] or [[degree]], or {{lb|en|by extension}}, a [[peak]] or highest degree. #* '''September 28, 1710''', {{w|Joseph Addison}}, ''Whig-Examiner'' No. 2 #* {{quote-book|en|year=1748|author=w:David Hume|title={{w|An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding|Enquiries concerning the human understanding and concerning the principles of moral}}|publisher=Oxford University Press|year_published=1973|section=11 |passage=But, except the mind be disordered by disease or madness, they never can arrive at such a '''pitch''' of vivacity}} #* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=5|passage=In the eyes of Mr. Farquhar Fenelon Cooke the apotheosis of the Celebrity was complete. The people of Asquith were not only willing to attend the house-warming, but had been worked up to the '''pitch''' of eagerness.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2014|author=James Booth|title=Philip Larkin: Life, Art and Love|page=190 |passage=In this poem his 'vernacular' bluster and garish misrhymes build to a '''pitch''' of rowdy anarchy {{...}}}} # A point or peak; the extreme point of elevation or depression. #* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=2|passage=Driven headlong from the '''pitch''' of heaven, down / Into this deep.|year=1873}} # The most [[thrust]]-out point of a [[headland]] or [[cape]]. # {{lb|en|obsolete|uncountable}} Collectively, the [[outermost]] [[point]]s of some part of the [[body]], especially the [[shoulder]]s or [[hip]]s. #* {{RQ:Marlowe Tamburlaine|part=1|scene=i|page=28|passage=Such breadth of ſhoulders as might mainely beare
Olde ''Atlas'' burthen, twixt his manly '''pitch''',
A pearle more worth, then all the world is plaſte:}} # The [[height]] a [[bird]] [[reach]]es in [[flight]], especially a [[bird of prey]] preparing to [[swoop]] down on its [[prey]]. # {{lb|en|now|_|British|regional}} A person's or animal's [[height]]. #* {{RQ:Burton Melancholy|edition=2nd|part=II|section=3|member=2|passage=Alba the emperor was crook-backed, Epictetus lame; that great Alexander a little man of stature, Augustus Cæsar of the same '''pitch''' {{...}}.}} #* {{RQ:Butler Hudibras|year=1905|passage=So like in person, garb, and '''pitch''',
'Twas hard t' interpret which was which}} # Prominence; importance. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Hamlet|act=III|scene=i|passage=Enterprises of great '''pitch''' and moment.}} # {{lb|en|climbing}} A section of a climb or rock face; specifically, the climbing distance between [[belay]]s or [[stance]]s. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1967|author=Anthony Greenbank|title=Instructions in Mountaineering|page=84 |passage=You [[lead through|lead "through"]] instead — your companion leads a '''pitch''', then you join him. But instead of swapping over at the ice axe belay, you carry on in the lead, cutting or kicking steps until you are about twenty feet above.}} # {{lb|en|caving}} A vertical cave passage, only negotiable by using rope or ladders. #: {{ux|en|The entrance '''pitch''' requires 30 metres of rope.}} # {{lb|en|cricket}} That point of the ground on which the ball pitches or [[light]]s when bowled.
